text:
Toronto hosts Edmonton on Saturday night in a very different frame of mind from the last meeting, when the Maple Leafs won 7-2 on Oct 24. They are 0-5-0 since, outscored 22-9, and fell 5-2 to Minnesota two days ago, when Matt Boldy scored three. They are missing Kirill Marchenko (14 points in 14 games), with John Tavares moving beside Paul and Nylander and Jack Roslovic up to 19:34 a night. The Oilers have won three straight, most recently 3-2 over Philadelphia on an Evan Bouchard overtime goal, without Isaac Howard. Our numbers say their results run ahead of their chances.

Neither side has controlled play at five on five: EDM has 48% of the expected goals (a measure of chance quality), TOR 46%. Edmonton's power play creates 0.81 expected goals a game and Toronto's penalty kill allows 0.78, while the Leafs take 4.2 penalties a game. In net, projected starter Devon Levi is 1.5 goals above expected this season, while Sergei Bobrovsky is 1.3 below, after 13.5 below last year.

Connor McDavid, on a 20-game point streak, is at 93% for a point and 42% to score. Leon Draisaitl is at 50% to score. Zach Hyman is one point from 500 and has Toronto ties. For Toronto, we have Auston Matthews at 37% to score, and Roslovic has 14 points in 10 games. Our under-the-radar pick is Colton Dach, a third-liner with 2.1 expected goals in his last 10 games, at 16% to score.
